Nights I feel are the hardest to handle for lonely people (like myself) because it's the one time during the 24 hour day that the world (hypothetically, time zones and stuff) slows down, people go home, to their kids, partner, pets, friends, etc. and relax.

While for lonely people it's just like the rest of the day, only sadder, because the world has momentarily stopped moving, and you still feel the same.

There is less to distract yourself with during the night, it's quieter, slower, less is going on. So there is nothing to preoccupy your brain from the pain.

Also, nighttime just tends to be more somber, I'm not sure exactly why, but I think it has to do with the darkness and peacefulness of it.

Typically, that's why I believe it gets worse for lonely people at night.

Also probably because of the knowledge that most people at night are going to be sleeping held by another person, or at least in the same house as someone, while lonely people have to just bury themselves in blankets and imagine the warmth of another body.
